title: The corner, ii
logline: Wagner's is empty. The strip is about the Grunion Run. The empty windows are behind everything.

panels.composition: Main street at dusk, Grunion night; townspeople walking toward the beach with buckets. GULLY with the thermos. WOOD with BARNABY in his arms. Behind them: Wagner's, dark, windows papered.

balloons.text: You carrying him the whole way?

image.prompt: a small-town main street at dusk with townspeople carrying buckets toward a beach, a man with a thermos, another carrying an old dog, and behind them a dark hardware store with papered-over windows, muddy watercolor

panels.composition: The papered window. A single sheet of paper taped inside, hand-lettered: THANK YOU SMALL WOOD 1962–2011.
props: a taped note in the window

image.prompt: close-up of a papered-over storefront window with a single hand-lettered thank-you note taped inside
image.notes: THANK YOU SMALL WOOD 1962–2011. Letter after. The only time the strip's background says a date.

panels.composition: Wood, passing it, glancing. The dog glancing. Gully not.

image.prompt: two men passing a dark storefront at dusk, one and the dog he carries glancing at it, the other looking ahead, no words

panels.composition: The beach ahead. Lanterns starting. The corner behind them, dark. The strip walks into the Grunion Run and the book takes the rest as one strip elsewhere.

image.prompt: two men and a dog walking toward a beach where lanterns are being lit at dusk, a dark storefront corner behind them, watercolor, no words

art.line: brush-pen; the flats cleaner; the Sundays the point now

notes: Wagner's: THANK YOU SMALL WOOD 1962–2011. The strip glances once.
